props.gloss_en: Rava: over the farmers' riheta, to which they add much flour, one blesses 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
the reason: the flour is the primary ingredient
Rava: over Mechoza's riheta, which has little flour, one blesses 'by Whose word all things came to be'
the reason: the honey is the primary ingredient
Rava, reversing himself: over both this and that riheta one blesses 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
Rav and Shmuel: over anything containing any of the five species one blesses 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
Rav Yosef: over chavitza containing olive-size crumbs, at the start one blesses 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
...and at the end the three blessings
Rav Yosef: over chavitza without olive-size crumbs, at the start one blesses 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
...and at the end one blessing abridged from the three
the baraita: one standing and offering meal-offerings in Jerusalem says 'Who has given us life, sustained us and brought us to this time'
the baraita: taking them to eat, he blesses 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
taught on it: and all of them, he crumbles them into olive-bulk pieces
the tanna of R' Yishmael's school: he crushes them until he returns them to their flour
the baraita: one who gathered an olive-bulk from all of them and ate it -- if chametz, he is liable to karet; if matza, one fulfils his obligation with it on Pesach
the same baraita's final clause: provided he ate them within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
the baraita speaks of where he kneaded the crumbs together [into one mass]
rather, the baraita speaks of crumbs that came from a large loaf
Rav Sheshet: over chavitza, even though it has no olive-size crumbs, one blesses 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
Rava: provided it has the appearance of bread
and terokanin are obligated in challa (voice: see header)
R' Yochanan (brought by Ravin): terokanin are exempt from challa
Abaye: terokanin are kuba de'ara (dough baked in a pit in the ground)
Abaye: terita is exempt from challa
some say: terita is dough poured onto a boiling surface
and some say: Indian bread
and some say: bread made for kutach
R' Chiyya taught: bread made for kutach is exempt from challa
a baraita: [bread made for kutach] is obligated in challa
R' Yehuda: its making proves [what it is for]
R' Yehuda: if he made them thick, they are obligated
R' Yehuda: if like boards, they are exempt
Rav Yosef (asked by Abaye): do you think it is bread? it is mere dough, and one blesses over it 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
Rav Yosef's reason: it is mere kneaded dough, not bread
Mar Zutra made his meal on it and blessed over it 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
...and the three blessings after it
Mar bar Rav Ashi: a person fulfils his [matza] obligation on Pesach with them
the reason: we call it 'bread of affliction'
Mar bar Rav Ashi: over date honey one blesses 'by Whose word all things came to be'
the reason: it is mere exudation [of the fruit]
the mishnah: date honey, apple wine, winter-grape vinegar and other fruit juices of teruma -- R' Eliezer obligates [a non-priest who drank them] in the principal and a fifth
and R' Yehoshua exempts
whose view is Mar bar Rav Ashi's? that of 'this tanna' of the mishnah -- the one who exempts, R' Yehoshua
one of the Rabbis to Rava: terima -- what is its law? (Rava did not grasp the word; Ravina asked the asker: do you mean sesame, safflower or grape-pit terima?)
Rava: certainly you mean something pounded
Rav Asi: from dates of teruma one may make terima
Rav Asi: and one may not make beer from them
the halakha: over dates made into terima one blesses 'Who creates fruit of the tree'
the reason: they remain in their state as at first
shetita: Rav said 'by Whose word all things came to be'
and Shmuel said 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
Rav Chisda: they do not disagree -- this [Shmuel's] is of thick shetita
Rav Chisda: ...and this [Rav's] is of thin shetita
Rav Chisda: thick, they make it for eating
Rav Chisda: thin, they make it for healing
the baraita: and they agree that one may stir shetita on Shabbat and drink Egyptian zithom
the mishnah: all foods a person may eat for healing on Shabbat, and all drinks he may drink
Abaye: [there] the man intends eating; here too the man intends eating
Abaye, the other version: the man intends eating and the healing comes of itself; so too here

Rav and Shmuel's statement is needed: from the baraita alone I would say [blessing only where] one intends eating and healing comes of itself; here, intending healing from the outset, one would not bless at all
it teaches: since he has pleasure from it, he must bless

supports.gloss_en: דרב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו: כל שיש בו מחמשת המינים מברכין עליו בורא מיני מזונות
מנא אמינא לה -- דתניא: נטלן לאכלן מברך המוציא לחם מן הארץ (joined with the ותני עלה clause, next edge)
ותני עלה: וכולן פותתן כזית -- so olive-size crumbs are what receive hamotzi
כמאן? כי האי תנא, דתנן: ...רבי אליעזר מחייב קרן וחומש ורבי יהושע פוטר -- date honey is not the fruit itself

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה -- for the tanna of R' Yishmael's school, who crushes the meal-offerings back to flour, would one not bless hamotzi? וכי תימא הכי נמי -- והתניא: an olive-bulk gathered from all the crumbs is matza with which one fulfils on Pesach (and chametz liable to karet): crumbs smaller than an olive-bulk are still bread

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא הכא במאי עסקינן -- בבא מלחם גדול: the baraita's crumbs came from a large loaf (= p_okimta_lechem_gadol). The first answer, בשעירסן (37b.8, = p_okimta_sheeirsan), fell to אימא סיפא and was surrendered

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי אימא סיפא: והוא שאכלן בכדי אכילת פרס -- if kneaded into one mass, 'שאכלן' (ate them) should read 'שאכלו' (ate it)
והא תניא: חייב בחלה -- but a baraita obligates bread made for kutach in challa!

answered_by.gloss_en: התם כדקתני טעמא: רבי יהודה אומר מעשיה מוכיחין עליה -- עשאן כעבין חייבין, כלמודין פטורים (38a.1): that baraita distinguishes by the shape of the making (= p_maaseha_mochichin, p_keavin_chayavin, p_kelimudin_peturin)

objections.gloss_en: מתיב רב יוסף: ושוין שבוחשין את השתות בשבת ושותין זיתום המצרי -- ואי סלקא דעתך לרפואה קא מכוין, רפואה בשבת מי שרי?!

answered_by.gloss_en: ואת לא תסברא? והא תנן: כל האוכלין אוכל אדם לרפואה בשבת (= p_kol_haochlin_lirfua) -- what you must say there, the man intends eating; here too the man intends eating (= p_gavra_laachila_mechaven)
לישנא אחרינא: he intends eating and the healing comes of itself; so too here (= p_refua_mimeila)

rulings.gloss_en: והלכתא: תמרי ועבדינהו טרימא מברכין עלייהו בורא פרי העץ
